domain: Monetary Policy / Digital Currency / Behavioral Economics
topic_summary: Analysis of 'Econographics' as both a behavioral economics methodology measuring trait-like economic decision-making patterns and an Atlantic Council publication series tracking digital currency developments, particularly China's e-CNY CBDC experiment and its geopolitical implications for dollar hegemony.

key_entities: People's Bank of China (PBOC) - central bank issuing e-CNY
Atlantic Council - policy research organization using 'Econographics' as publication category
Chapman/Dean/Ortoleva/Snowberg/Camerer - behavioral economics researchers defining econographics as trait measures
Project mBridge - wholesale CBDC cross-border settlement platform
BIS Innovation Hub - original incubator of mBridge, withdrew 2024
U.S. Federal Reserve - implicit competitor in CBDC/stablecoin space
Commercial stablecoins (Tether/USDC) - private digital money alternatives
Chinese tourists/merchants - retail e-CNY adoption vector
key_tensions: Behavioral regularities vs rational choice models (econographics as methodology challenges standard economics)
Sovereign digital currency vs private stablecoins (e-CNY as state answer to crypto)
Dollar hegemony vs multipolar monetary system (mBridge as parallel settlement rail)
key_claims: Econographics (behavioral) reduces 21 measures to 6 principal components, revealing structure in economic decision-making
China's e-CNY grew 800% since 2023, reaching $2.3T cumulative transaction value by late 2025
Project mBridge volume increased 2,500-fold to $55.49B, with e-CNY comprising 95% of settlement
Interest-bearing e-CNY features move CBDC from payment instrument to savings-adjacent asset
PBOC frames e-CNY within vision for 'multipolar international monetary system' as counterweight to dollar weaponization
146 countries representing 98% of global GDP exploring CBDCs, with 77 in advanced phase
key_mechanisms: Principal component analysis reducing behavioral measures to underlying structure
E-CNY distribution through commercial banks with PBOC oversight via dual operations centers
Project mBridge direct central bank settlement bypassing correspondent banking
Interest-bearing CBDC features competing with stablecoins within regulated framework
key_absences: No discussion of whether behavioral econographics correlate with CBDC adoption patterns
Missing analysis of how consumer spending profiles (econography definition 1) inform CBDC design
Absent treatment of whether U.S. will pursue CBDC or rely on stablecoin regulation

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: What constitutes legitimate digital money in a sovereign monetary system
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Central bank monopoly on legal tender issuance vs market-driven private money innovation

readings.commitment: Legitimate digital money must be state-issued legal tender under central bank control
readings.authority_grounding: Monetary sovereignty doctrine; central bank as lender of last resort
readings.expected_structural_delta: State visibility into all transactions; programmable money with policy-embedded rules; beneficiary is state fiscal/monetary control; victim is financial privacy

readings.commitment: Legitimate digital money can be privately issued if regulated and backed by sovereign currency reserves
readings.authority_grounding: Banking regulation precedent; deposit insurance frameworks
readings.expected_structural_delta: Private innovation within regulatory perimeter; beneficiary is payment efficiency and financial inclusion; victim is monetary policy transmission (leakage to private issuers)

readings.commitment: Legitimate digital money emerges from decentralized consensus without state permission
readings.authority_grounding: Cryptographic proof; network effects; censorship resistance
readings.expected_structural_delta: No central authority; beneficiary is individual financial sovereignty; victim is state capacity for capital controls and sanctions enforcement

axiom_contradictions.basis: Sovereign CBDC axiom requires state monopoly on legitimate money issuance; crypto axiom requires money legitimacy independent of state permission. No coherent framework holds both simultaneously.

axes.structural_delta: Competing foundations for what makes digital money legitimate in sovereign monetary systems
axes.primary_observable: Regulatory treatment of CBDCs vs stablecoins vs crypto; cross-border settlement volume by instrument type
axes.selection_reason: Contested kernel with three distinct readings; highest centrality as upstream to both geopolitical and adoption axes

axes.human_readable: Geopolitical Settlement Competition (Dollar Hegemony vs Parallel Rails)
axes.structural_delta: Competition between dollar-based correspondent banking and alternative settlement infrastructure
axes.primary_observable: mBridge transaction volume; share of trade settled outside SWIFT; central bank reserve currency composition
axes.selection_reason: Distinct observable (settlement infrastructure topology) independent of legitimacy kernel; downstream synthesis of sovereign_cbdc_reading implications

axes.human_readable: Behavioral Adoption Friction (Econographic Trait Barriers to CBDC Use)
axes.structural_delta: Mismatch between CBDC design assumptions and actual economic decision-making patterns
axes.primary_observable: Correlation between econographic principal components and e-CNY wallet activation/usage rates
axes.selection_reason: Bridges behavioral econographics methodology to CBDC adoption; different observable than geopolitical axis; coordination problem not extraction

axes.human_readable: Interest-Bearing CBDC Innovation (Deposit-Like Features in Sovereign Digital Money)
axes.structural_delta: CBDC transition from pure payment instrument to savings-adjacent asset via interest features
axes.primary_observable: E-CNY interest rate policy; household allocation between bank deposits and e-CNY wallets
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: implementation detail of sovereign_cbdc_reading rather than independent axis; captured in that reading's constraint story

axes.human_readable: Privacy-Efficiency Tradeoff (Transaction Visibility vs Payment Speed)
axes.structural_delta: Inverse relationship between state transaction visibility and user financial privacy
axes.primary_observable: E-CNY transaction metadata granularity; user wallet adoption rates by privacy-sensitive demographics
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: physical constraint of digital payment systems; feeds into kernel but lower centrality than selected axes

deferred_axes.structural_delta: CBDC transition from payment instrument to savings-adjacent asset
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Implementation detail of sovereign_cbdc_reading; interest-bearing features are mechanism within that reading's constraint story rather than independent axis

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Inverse relationship between transaction visibility and financial privacy
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Physical constraint of digital payment systems; lower centrality than selected axes; feeds into kernel but captured implicitly in sovereign_cbdc_reading victim structure

omegas.description: Does behavioral econographics (trait-like decision patterns) predict CBDC adoption? No research links the Chapman et al. principal components to digital currency usage. If risk aversion or time preference clusters correlate with e-CNY wallet activation, the behavioral methodology becomes predictive tool for CBDC design.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) - missing link between two definitions of econographics

omegas.description: Will U.S. pursue CBDC or rely on regulated stablecoins? Input describes conflicting policy agendas but no resolution. If U.S. chooses stablecoin regulation over CBDC, the regulated_stablecoin_reading becomes dominant Western model; if CBDC, sovereign_cbdc_reading becomes global norm.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) - U.S. policy choice determines which reading captures dollar system evolution

omegas.description: Why did BIS withdraw from mBridge governance in October 2024? Input notes transfer to partner central banks but no explanation. If withdrawal signals Western concern about sanctions evasion, mBridge becomes explicitly geopolitical; if technical handoff, remains neutral infrastructure.

Do regulated_stablecoin and sovereign_cbdc readings collapse if stablecoins become fully reserve-backed and supervised like narrow banks? If regulatory convergence eliminates structural difference, kernel reduces to two readings (state vs permissionless).
omegas.source: §1.3-K coherence check - potential reading collapse under regulatory convergence scenario

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel decomposition applied successfully; three readings pass individually-holdable test with distinct authority groundings and structural deltas. Geopolitical and behavioral axes pass §3 pairwise independence test (different observables, different beneficiary structures).
